body.p: REMARKS

By the amendments set forth supra, claim 2 has been canceled without prejudice and claims 1, 3, 6, and 7 have been amended. Accordingly, claims 1 and 3-9 are now pending in the above-referenced patent application and under examination. Applicant respectfully contends no issue of new matter has been presented by the amendments.
January 13 Telephone Interview

The courtesies extended to Applicant's representative by Examiner Dager at the interview held January 13, 2025, are appreciated. The reasons presented at the interview as warranting favorable action are incorporated into the remarks below, which constitute Applicant's record of the interview.
In the Non-Final Office Action:
Claims 1-91 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. §102(a)(2) as allegedly being anticipated by Ganguli et al. (U.S. Patent No. 11,541,910; hereinafter "Ganguli").
In reply to the rejection of claims 1 and 3-9 under 35 U.S.C. §102(a)(2) as allegedly being anticipated by Ganguli, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration.
Applicant respectfully submits that Ganguli does not teach or suggest every element of the claimed invention. Elements of claim 2 have been incorporated into claim

SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.242.087
rendering moot the rejection of this claim.
Regarding claim 1, claim 1 recites: a control device that performs travel control of a vehicle, the control device comprising:
a processor configured to acquire output information of a sensor
configured to detect an object in an around of the vehicle based on a
reflected wave from the object, wherein
the processor is configured to:
acquire detection point data of the object in a peripheral region of the vehicle based on the output information of the sensor;

recognize that a peripheral environment of the vehicle is a travel-restricted section based on a distribution of detection point data in a first group including a plurality pieces of the detection point data on one side in a left-right direction of the vehicle in the peripheral region; classify the first group into a plurality of first subgroups; and
recognize that the peripheral environment is the travel-restricted section based on a variation amount of positions of the plurality of first subgroups in the left- right direction. (emphasis added).

As discussed in the January 13 interview, the Office Action alleges that column 3, lines 31-49 of Ganguli teach the elements recited by dependent claim 2. Applicant respectfully disagrees. Ganguli discloses recognizing an angle and a distance of an object in a surrounding region (shoulder area) based on detection results of sensors, but fails to teach the feature recited in claim 1 of the present application that "the processor is configured to: classify the first group into a plurality of first subgroups; and recognize
that the peripheral environment is the travel-restricted section based on a variation amount of positions of the plurality of first subgroups in the left-right direction."

To assist the Examiner's understanding, explanation is now made in reference to a non-limiting embodiment of Applicant's disclosure, in which, in the present invention, since the travel-restricted section is recognized based on the variation amount in the positions of the two first subgroups in the left-right direction, the recognition can be performed at high speed and with high accuracy, as described in paragraph [0099] of the U.S. Pre-Grant Publication of the present application (paragraph [0082] of the original disclosure).

Accordingly, as agreed to in the January 13 interview, Ganguli clearly does not teach or suggest, inter alia, that "the processing is configured to ... classify the first group into a plurality of first subgroups; and recognize that the peripheral environment is the travel-restricted section based on a variation amount of positions of the plurality of first subgroups in the left-right direction," as recited by amended claim 1.

Therefore, in view of the above deficiencies, Ganguli clearly fails to teach or suggest every element as recited by amended independent claim 1. At least for the aforementioned reasons, claim 1 is not anticipated by Ganguli under 35 U.S.C. §102(a)(2). Claims 3-9 are dependent claims that are each also patentably distinguished over Ganguli at least in view of their respective dependencies, as well as for their additionally recited elements.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection of claims 1 and 3-9 under 35 U.S.C. §102(a)(2).
CONCLUSION

Applicant believes that a full and complete response has been made to the Office Action and respectfully submits that all of the stated objections and grounds for rejection have been overcome or rendered moot. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that all pending claims are allowable and that the application is in condition for allowance.

Should the Examiner feel that there are any issues outstanding after consideration of this response, the Examiner is invited to contact the Applicant's undersigned representative at the number below to expedite prosecution.
Prompt and favorable consideration of this Reply is respectfully requested.
